findings.title: The 'Two mounts are independent' test skips opening the sheet on the first root, which the scenario requires
findings.evidence: The scenario says that on the second root the player opens the sheet (stubbed `showPopover()`), marks 4×4 and presses «Почати», 'then on the first root the player does the same for «Поле 8×8»'. The test calls `openSheet(second)` and then, for the first root, only `markSize(first, 8); pressStart(first);` without `openSheet(first)`. In jsdom this probably makes no difference to the result. But the test does not follow the scenario's steps, and it would not notice a regression where opening one root's sheet changes shared state (the shared `languageMounts` set shows that mounts do share module state).
findings.suggestion: Add `openSheet(first);` before `markSize(first, 8);` so the test performs the scenario's steps exactly.
verifierNotes: The spec scenario (openspec/changes/update-panel-shell/specs/play-page/spec.md:562-568) says that on the second root the player opens the sheet, marks a size and presses «Почати». It then says "on the first root the player does the same", which includes opening the sheet. The test at tests/play-page-root-size.test.ts:156-165 calls openSheet(second) but goes straight to markSize(first, 8) and pressStart(first) with no openSheet(first). So the deviation is real. Other tests in the same file (lines 79-86) also call markSize and pressStart without openSheet, so in jsdom the omission most likely changes nothing and the test would still pass. The only effect is a small loss of fidelity to the scenario. That is a test-completeness nit with very low impact, so I confirm the finding at minor severity or below.

The finding is accurate but trivial. The scenario is at openspec/changes/update-panel-shell/specs/play-page/spec.md:565. It says that on the second root the player opens the sheet, marks 4×4 and presses «Почати», and that "then on the first root the player does the same for «Поле 8×8»". "The same" includes opening the sheet. The test at tests/play-page-root-size.test.ts lines 153-157 calls openSheet(second) but goes straight to markSize(first, 8); pressStart(first) without openSheet(first). The omission is real. It affects only the test's fidelity to the scenario, not any real user or attacker, and the test most likely still passes. Nothing in the product can fail because of it, so I rate it a low-severity test nit and keep it as reported.
findings.disposition: fixed in fix round 1: openSheet(first) added (tests/play-page-root-size.test.ts)

findings.title: e2e shell test pins fill and border to the spec values, but never checks the design's shadow against the spec's rgba(0,0,0,0.18)/0.25
findings.evidence: Lines 360-361 assert `want.surface.fill` equals `FILL[scheme]` and `want.surface.border` equals the spec border. The shadow is only compared page-vs-design: `note('box-shadow', shadowDifference(have.surface.shadow, want.surface.shadow))`. The spec scenario names the expected layers (`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.18)` below 48rem on the three panels, `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25)` from 48rem and on the dialog). If the design build and the page drifted together (for example after a design rebuild), the shadow check would still pass. The fill and border cannot drift this way because they are anchored.
findings.suggestion: Add a spec anchor for the design side: parse `want.surface.shadow` and assert the alpha (0.18 or 0.25, by surface and viewport) and the geometry (0 -8px 32px 0 or 0 16px 40px 0). Do the same for the strip shadow.
verifierNotes: The facts are accurate. Lines 360-361 anchor fill and border to literals, and line 370 compares shadow only page against design. But this is not an incorrect mechanism. The spec scenario (update-panel-shell play-page spec, line 507) says the shadow "equals the design's layer by layer" with the same colour (alpha within 0.005) and the same offsets, blur and spread. The rgba(0,0,0,0.18) and 0.25 values are parenthetical illustrations of the design's values, not a separate literal requirement. shadowDifference compares exactly those things. The file header says the design is read live as the reference, and the anchors on fill and border exist as an extra guard. The finding describes an optional hardening of a test, an extra anchor against a design rebuild drifting. It does not describe a wrong check, and it doesn't show how the page could ship with a shadow the spec forbids. The finding's own rating is minor severity and low confidence. I'm refuting it as a correctness defect.

Confirmed at line 370: the design shadow is only compared page-vs-design. Fill and border are anchored to spec literals at lines 360-361, but no test in e2e or tests pins the shadow alpha or geometry to the spec values. The gap is real. It is a test-coverage weakness, not a user-facing defect. It only matters if the page and the design build drift together, and the design build is a frozen, locally served output. Minor severity and low confidence fit.
findings.disposition: contested, treated as confirmed and fixed: the e2e anchors the design's shadow to the spec's literal (0.18 sheet below 48rem, 0.25 panel and dialog); 24 of 24 green

findings.title: Size-dependent layout variables are now keyed on #app only, so .board is no longer self-contained under any other mount root
findings.evidence: `--n`, `--cell-max`, `--board-gap`, `--board-pad` and `--board-width` moved from `.board` to `#app { --n: 6; ... }` and `#app[data-size='4'|'8']`, while `.board` still uses `grid-template-columns: repeat(var(--n), minmax(0, 1fr))` and `width: min(100%, var(--board-width), ...)`. `mountPlayPage(root)` accepts any element and does set `data-size` on it, but if that element is not `#app`, `--n` is undefined. The grid declaration is then invalid at computed-value time and the board collapses to one column. Before this change the board read its own `data-size`. The spec allows this ('the layout rules key on #app, the one root the page is built for'), so it does not break the spec. But it couples layout to an id while the JS hook is generic.
findings.suggestion: Accept and document it, as the spec does. Or key the variable rules on the hook instead of the id (for example `[data-size='8']:has(> .board-host)` is not allowed, but a class the page puts on its root, such as `.play-root[data-size='8']`, would work). Then any mounted root gets the variables, and the e2e/jsdom roots match production.
verifierNotes: The mechanism is literally true: --n and the other size variables are declared only on #app, so a mount root that is not #app would get an invalid grid. But it is not a correctness defect. The only production caller is src/main.ts, which mounts into the #app element from index.html. The file already declares the other layout variables (--space-*) on #app and says so in its comment, so the id coupling is an established convention. The spec explicitly allows it, as the finding concedes. The finding names no reachable failure path. It only notes that jsdom test roots may differ, and the layout tests that read the stylesheet do not depend on the root. This is a design preference, not a wrong-behaviour bug.

The only production caller is src/main.ts, which calls mountPlayPage(app) on the #app element from index.html (line 40). The #app rule therefore always applies for real users, and no attacker or user can pick a different mount root. The other callers are jsdom tests (tests/helpers/play-page.ts and tests/play-page-root-size.test.ts), and jsdom does no layout, so the missing --n has no effect there. The finding itself says the spec allows this and describes it as coupling, not a defect. It cannot occur in practice, so it is not exploitable or reproducible.
findings.disposition: rejected by the verifiers; no change

findings.title: A missing page-side close button or strip crashes the e2e case instead of being reported as a labelled difference
findings.evidence: `note('«Закрити» fill', colourDifference(have.closeFill ?? 'none', want.closeFill))` passes the string 'none' to `parseColour`. That function throws `not an rgb(a) colour: "none"` instead of returning a difference. Inside `read()`, `paintOf` also uses `page.locator(...).evaluate`, which times out when the close button is missing. The spec asks that 'a pair of values that differ is reported with the surface, the scheme, the viewport and both strings'. A throw loses the surface/scheme/viewport label that `differences` would carry.
findings.suggestion: In `read()`, return null when the close button or strip is missing (check with `locator.count()`). In the comparison, push an explicit `${label}: page has no element, design ${want...}` difference instead of calling `colourDifference` with 'none'.
verifierNotes: The mechanism is only partly real, and it doesn't amount to a defect. In `read()`, `closeFill` is null only when `CLOSE_BUTTON[surface]` is undefined. If the page lacks a close button that is configured, `page.locator(...).evaluate` times out inside `read()`. The error names the locator, and the `test()` title carries the surface, scheme and viewport. The test still fails loudly and is never silently green. The `'none'` fallback at line 371 can only run when `want.closeFill !== null` but the page-side selector is undefined. That is an internal config mismatch the spec author controls, and the thrown parse error would still fail the test. The claim that surface/scheme/viewport labels are lost is overstated. The test name supplies them, and only the in-message diff format differs. This is a stylistic nicety for failure reporting, not wrong behaviour, and the claimed mismatch with the spec's "differences reported" requirement is not clearly a violation. A missing element is an environment or setup failure, not a paint difference.

The 'none' path the finding cites cannot be reached. In `read()` (lines ~236-250), `closeFill` is null only when the surface has no `CLOSE_BUTTON` entry. The same `read()` and the same `surface` produce both the design reading and the page reading. So when `want.closeFill !== null`, `have.closeFill` is always a string, because `read()` either returns a computed colour or throws. The `?? 'none'` fallback is dead code, and `parseColour('none')` is never called. The same applies to `stripShadow`, and `parseShadow` handles 'none' anyway.

The remaining case is a page with no close button or strip. There, `page.locator(...).evaluate` times out inside `read()` and the test fails. That is a failing test with a locator-timeout message that names the selector, not a silent pass or a false green. The failure also shows up in Playwright's output under the test title, which already contains the scheme, surface and viewport (`${name}`). So the label is not lost. The only cost is a less tidy error message in a test-only helper, which is a style nit and not a correctness or reproducibility defect. The finding is low-confidence and minor, and its mechanism is mostly unreachable.
findings.disposition: rejected by the verifiers; no change
